status: A weekly summary prepared automatically from official data. It is a research product, not an official warning, and it has not been reviewed by an analyst.
overview: On 28 February 2026, war involving Iran led to the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. Still showing in the data: about 3 ships a day in the four weeks to 15 November 2026, against a typical 86 for this time of year.

In October 2026, the World Bank's fertilizer price index stood at 148 (2010 = 100), 6% higher than a year earlier. Prices: DAP US$803 a tonne; Urea US$420 a tonne. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years, in US dollars without adjusting for inflation. It is about 8% below the typical level.

Grain elevators and port terminals held 7.25 million tonnes of grain in the week ending 4 October 2026. That is higher than at this time of year in any of the past five years. It is about 2% above the typical level. Worth watching. One unusual reading does not mean a crisis. These are the latest figures published; the source has not updated as expected since.

Ports shipped 3.21 million tonnes of grain abroad in the four weeks to 4 October 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 4% above the typical level. These are the latest figures published; the source has not updated as expected since.

We follow 12 fresh fruits and vegetables at the Toronto wholesale market. In the latest week, two cost more and two cost less than at this time of year in any recent year, after allowing for inflation. Four are in their normal range, and for four we do not have enough past data. These are the latest figures published; the source has not updated as expected since.

In October 2026, grocery prices were 2.0% higher than a year earlier, and average hourly wages were 2.2% higher. Wages have risen faster than grocery prices for two months in a row. These are the latest figures published; the source has not updated as expected since.

The Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System, run by the United Nations and the European Commission, lists eight serious disasters around the world. Three are in countries Canada buys food or farm supplies from. That tells us where to look; it does not mean Canada is affected.

conditions.title: Grain shipped through ports
conditions.text: Ports shipped 3.21 million tonnes of grain abroad in the four weeks to 4 October 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 4% above the typical level.

conditions.title: Fresh fruit and vegetable prices
conditions.text: We follow 12 fresh fruits and vegetables at the Toronto wholesale market. In the latest week, two cost more and two cost less than at this time of year in any recent year, after allowing for inflation. Four are in their normal range, and for four we do not have enough past data.

conditions.title: Grocery prices compared with wages
conditions.text: In October 2026, grocery prices were 2.0% higher than a year earlier, and average hourly wages were 2.2% higher. Wages have risen faster than grocery prices for two months in a row.

conditions.title: Food recalls
conditions.text: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency issued 21 food recall notices in the 30 days to 20 November 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 12% below the typical level.

conditions.title: Weather warnings
conditions.text: 17 weather alerts were in effect in seven provinces or territories when we last checked, including 11 warnings.

conditions.title: Ships through key sea lanes
conditions.text: Ships through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 3 a day over the four weeks to 15 November 2026. In the same weeks of the past five years the typical figure was about 86 a day. That is below the range of every one of those years, about 96% below the typical level. Also unusual: Bab el-Mandeb Strait (fewer ships than usual).

conditions.title: Cargo loaded at Canadian ports
conditions.text: Ships loaded an estimated 1.5 million tonnes a week at the Port of Vancouver in the four weeks to 13 November 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 8% above the typical level. Elsewhere, unusual: Montreal (more than usual).

conditions.title: World fertilizer prices
conditions.text: In October 2026, the World Bank's fertilizer price index stood at 148 (2010 = 100), 6% higher than a year earlier. Prices: DAP US$803 a tonne; Urea US$420 a tonne. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years, in US dollars without adjusting for inflation. It is about 8% below the typical level.

conditions.title: World food and energy prices
conditions.text: In October 2026, the World Bank's food price index stood at 122 (2010 = 100), 15% higher than a year earlier. Energy prices were 89% higher than a year earlier. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years, in US dollars without adjusting for inflation.

conditions.title: Diesel prices
conditions.text: Diesel at self-serve pumps averaged 262.9 cents a litre across five cities in October 2026, 71% more than a year earlier. That is higher than at this time of year in any of the past five years, after allowing for inflation. It is about 51% above the typical level. Worth watching. One unusual reading does not mean a crisis.

conditions.title: What farmers pay for inputs
conditions.text: In the quarter starting April 2026, the prices Canadian farmers paid for all inputs stood at 187 on Statistics Canada's index (2020 = 100), 11% higher than a year earlier. Fertilizer alone was 24% higher. That is higher than at this time of year in any of the past five years. It is about 20% above the typical level. Worth watching. One unusual reading does not mean a crisis.

conditions.title: Store prices for everyday foods
conditions.text: We follow 15 everyday foods in Canadian stores. In September 2026, two cost more and three cost less than in the same month of any of the past five years, after allowing for inflation. Higher than usual: ground beef, whole chicken.

conditions.title: Grocery price rises by province
conditions.text: In October 2026, grocery prices were up most in Quebec (+3.0% on a year earlier) and least in Prince Edward Island (+0.1%). The national figure was +2.0%.

conditions.title: People who struggle to afford food
conditions.text: In 2024, 24.0% of people in the ten provinces lived in a household that struggled to afford food, up from 16.8% in 2018. Among children it was 30.8%. This survey is published once a year, more than a year after the fact.

conditions.title: Grain and fertilizer moved by rail
conditions.text: Railways carried 3.8 million tonnes of wheat, other grains and canola in August 2026. That is higher than at this time of year in any of the past five years. It is about 80% above the typical level. Worth watching. One unusual reading does not mean a crisis.

conditions.title: Strikes and lockouts
conditions.text: There were 68 strikes and lockouts under way in Canada in August 2026, five of them in transportation. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 24% above the typical level.

conditions.title: The Canadian dollar
conditions.text: One US dollar cost $1.42 Canadian on average so far in November 2026, 0.8% more than a year earlier. A weaker Canadian dollar makes imported food and farm inputs dearer. That is higher than at this time of year in any of the past five years. It is about 3% above the typical level. Worth watching. One unusual reading does not mean a crisis.

conditions.title: Drought on the Prairies
conditions.text: At the end of October 2026, 37% of southern Alberta, 0% of southern Saskatchewan and 25% of southern Manitoba were in moderate drought or worse. In Alberta, the province with the most drought, that is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past three years. It is about 52% below the typical level.

conditions.title: Drought where imported produce grows
conditions.text: In the week of 17 November 2026, 9% of California; 9% of Arizona; 7% of Florida; 59% of Washington was in moderate drought or worse. Unusual for the time of year: Arizona (less drought than in any of the past five years).

global.title: Tropical Cyclone MURASU-26
global.text: India supplied 27% of the rice Canada imported in 2025. We do not yet know whether this disaster affects that supply.

global.title: Tropical Cyclone ARNAB-26
global.text: India supplied 27% of the rice Canada imported in 2025. We do not yet know whether this disaster affects that supply.

gaps: Statistics Canada: the latest update failed, so we show data up to 1 October 2026.
Canadian Grain Commission: the newest data (4 October 2026) are older than this source usually is.
questions: There is more grain in storage than in any recent year at this time. Is that a comfortable reserve, or grain waiting for trains and ships?

Wholesale prices for strawberries from the United States and peppers from Ontario are higher than in any recent year at this time. Is the cause weather where they are grown, the exchange rate, or something else?
Fewer ships than usual are passing through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Which Canadian imports and exports use these routes, and what are the alternatives?
Diesel costs more than at this time in any recent year, after inflation. How much of that reaches farm costs and grocery prices, and how soon?

stress_test.title: Fertilizer imports are cut before seeding
